chunks: My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Abdillah al-Khorasani from al-Husayn ibn Salim from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Any person who grows up in his community, and then is not disciplined for his disobedience/sin, then indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, the first thing with which He punishes them is that He reduces their sustenance.
ai.seo_question: What is the divine consequence for a community that fails to discipline its sinners?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, this hadith highlights the sociological dimension of divine justice, where communal negligence in enforcing moral discipline triggers a tangible economic consequence. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that social cohesion and spiritual health are intertwined, with the failure to curb public sin leading directly to the diminishment of *rizq* (sustenance) as a primary, visible sign of divine displeasure.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to us by Sa’d b. Abdillah from Muhammad b. al-Hussain b. Abi al-Khattab from Abdillah al-Khorasani from al-Hussain b. Salim from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “If a person brought up in his community commits sins and people do not punish him from his crimes, the first chastisement from Allah upon them is that their sustenance will be reduced.”
